extracted.intended_audience: school and university administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and legal counsel implementing Title IX regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for educational institution recipients on how to comply with the Department's Title IX final regulations governing reporting, response, supportive measures, formal complaints, investigations, hearings, and protections for parties and witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator contact information and public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must include an email address for the Title IX Coordinator and require all the contact information for the Title IX Coordinator to be posted on the recipient's website. Recipients must notify all students, employees, parents/guardians of elementary and secondary students, and others of the Title IX Coordinator's contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(a); §106.8(b)(2). Contact information must include an office address, telephone number, and email address; recipients must prominently display that contact information on the recipient's website so that any person has a clear, accessible method of reporting sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any person may report (methods and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may report sexual harassment using the Title IX Coordinator's listed contact information whether or not the person reporting is the person alleged to be the victim, and reports may be made at any time (including during non-business hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports may be made in person, by mail, phone, email, or by any other method that results in the Title IX Coordinator receiving the person's verbal or written report. The final regulations expressly state reporting may occur by telephone number or electronic mail address, or by mail to the office address listed for the Title IX Coordinator. §106.8(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of actual knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual knowledge means notice of sexual harassment or allegations of sexual harassment to a recipient's Title IX Coordinator or any official of the recipient who has authority to institute corrective measures on behalf of the recipient, or to any employee of an elementary and secondary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.30. The mere ability or obligation to report sexual harassment, or having been trained to report, does not qualify an individual as one who has authority to institute corrective measures on behalf of the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint: who may file and what constitutes a filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal complaint may be filed by a complainant or signed by a Title IX Coordinator; signing a formal complaint by the Title IX Coordinator does not make the Title IX Coordinator a complainant or otherwise a party in the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.30. The definition of a 'document filed by a complainant' was broadened to include documents or electronic submissions (such as an email or online portal submission) that contain the complainant's physical or digital signature or otherwise indicate that the complainant is the person filing the formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient's prompt, non-deliberately indifferent response obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient has actual knowledge of sexual harassment in the recipient's education program or activity, the recipient must respond promptly and in a manner that is not clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(a). Required elements include offering supportive measures to the complainant, informing the complainant of the availability of supportive measures with or without filing a formal complaint, considering the complainant's wishes with respect to supportive measures, and explaining how to file a formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures: offering and implementation responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to the complainant with or without the filing of a formal complaint; the Title IX Coordinator is responsible for the effective implementation of supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(a); §106.30. Supportive measures may be implemented by other employees or administrators but require coordination (examples: no-contact orders, notifying campus security, registrar changes, adjusting academic requirements). Title IX Coordinator must promptly contact the complainant to discuss availability and consider the complainant's wishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant autonomy and protection when not participating
rubrics_metrics.description: Every complainant retains the right to refuse to participate in a grievance process; recipients must prohibit retaliation and specifically protect the right of any individual who chooses not to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.71 prohibits retaliation. If a grievance process is initiated contrary to a complainant's wishes (e.g., Title IX Coordinator signs a complaint), the recipient must treat the complainant as a party and send required notices, while protecting the complainant's right not to participate and avoid pressuring them to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator discretion to sign a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator may sign a formal complaint and initiate a §106.45 grievance process, but the decision to do so is discretionary and evaluated based on whether not initiating a grievance process would be clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations clarify that when a Title IX Coordinator signs a complaint despite a complainant's unwillingness to proceed, the Coordinator must remain free from conflicts of interest and bias and the recipient must respect the complainant's wishes regarding participation. See §106.8(a), §106.30, §106.45(b)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof rests on the recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of proof in the grievance process must rest on the recipient and not on the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(5)(i). This is an express allocation of the burden for gathering and weighing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to gather, present, and review evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties must be provided equal opportunity to gather, present, and review relevant evidence, including access to evidence, notice of interviews, and investigatory materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations provide that parties receive a copy of evidence for inspection and review, written notice of requested interviews, a copy of the investigative report, written notice of any hearing, and a copy of the written determination regarding responsibility; parties may note passage-of-time effects on evidence and argue about evidentiary weight. See §106.45(b)(2) and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary dismissal where insufficient evidence or unidentified complainant
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has discretion to dismiss a formal complaint where specific circumstances prevent the recipient from meeting its burden to gather sufficient evidence to reach a determination regarding responsibility (e.g., complainant identity unknown or unavailability of evidence due to passage of time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(3)(ii). If the complainant's identity is unknown or the recipient cannot gather sufficient evidence (e.g., because a reporter refuses to identify the complainant), the recipient's response is judged by whether it was clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: No disciplinary sanctions against respondent absent grievance process (with limited exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must treat respondents equitably by not imposing disciplinary sanctions or other actions that are not 'supportive measures' against a respondent without first following the §106.45 grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include emergency removal of a respondent from an education program or activity (§106.44(c)) and placing a non-student employee respondent on administrative leave during an investigation (§106.44(d)). §106.44(a) and §106.45(b)(1)(i) govern equitable treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal and administrative leave
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may be removed from an education program or activity on an emergency basis whether or not a grievance process is pending; a non-student employee respondent may be placed on administrative leave during the pendency of an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(c) (emergency removal); §106.44(d) (administrative leave). Such removals are exceptions to the general prohibition on imposing non-supportive disciplinary actions prior to following the grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX personnel must be free from conflicts of interest and trained
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and any person who facilitates informal resolution processes must be free from conflicts of interest and bias and trained, including training on how to serve impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(1)(iii) and related provisions. Training requirements are specified to ensure impartiality and competence in handling grievances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker independence from Title IX Coordinator and investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision-maker must be a different person from the Title IX Coordinator or investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(7) specifies separation of roles to reduce conflicts of interest; the final regulations do not preclude a Title IX Coordinator from also serving as the investigator, but the decision-maker must be separate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous and third-party reports: limits on response ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymous reports and third-party reports may trigger response obligations, but the nature of the recipient's non-deliberately indifferent response may depend on whether the report contains information identifying the alleged victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.30 and §106.44(a). If a reporter refuses to identify the complainant, the recipient may not be able to provide some elements of the required response (e.g., offering supportive measures) and may face limitations in gathering evidence; such circumstances may justify discretionary dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parents/guardians may act on behalf of complainant
rubrics_metrics.description: A parent or guardian with the legal right to act on a complainant's behalf may file a formal complaint on the complainant's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.6(g). Final regulations add §106.6(g) to acknowledge legal rights of parents/guardians to act on behalf of a complainant, respondent, or other party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality obligations and permitted disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must keep confidential the identity of any individual who has made a report or complaint of sex discrimination, including complainants, respondents, and witnesses, except as may be permitted by FERPA, required by law, or to the extent necessary to carry out the purposes of 34 CFR part 106 (including investigation, hearing, or judicial proceeding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.71(a). This provision both protects identities from disclosure and specifies narrow exceptions for necessary investigatory or legal disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental notice when complainant identity is discovered
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complainant's identity is discovered during the investigation, the recipient must send supplemental notice of allegations to the parties and treat the complainant as a party throughout the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(2)(ii). Without identification of the complainant at some point, a recipient may be unable to meet its burden to gather evidence sufficient to reach determination regarding responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible, simplified filing and broadened 'document filed by a complainant' definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'formal complaint' and 'document filed by a complainant' was revised to broaden what constitutes a written, signed document and to simplify and clarify the process for filing so it is more accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations indicate that electronic submissions (email, online portals) that contain a physical or digital signature or otherwise indicate the complainant is filing will qualify as a formal complaint; recipient procedures should reflect this accessibility.
